相比單簧管的溫和柔順，雙簧管音色更具穿透力與個性；與長笛的清脆明亮相比，雙簧管多: Compared with the mild smoothness of the clarinet, the oboe's timbre has more penetration and character; compared with the clear brightness of the flute, the oboe has a warmer, voice-like inner quality. 簧振氣鳴樂器是在霍恩博斯特爾-薩克斯樂器分類系統中發現的樂器類別之一。為了用這些: The reed aerophone is one of the instrument classes found in the Hornbostel-Sachs classification system. To make sound on these aerophones, the player's breath is directed at a thin blade, or at a pair of thin blades, which periodically interrupt the airflow and set the air moving.
簧振氣鳴樂器的起源可追溯至古代中東和地中海地區。最早的雙簧樂器出現在古埃及和古希: The reed aerophone can be traced back to the ancient Middle East and the Mediterranean. The earliest double-reed instruments appeared in ancient Egypt and ancient Greece, where musicians made reeds from strips of cane and produced a distinctive timbre. In the Middle Ages these instruments reached Europe through the Arab world and gradually developed into the modern oboe.
莫札特《雙簧管協奏曲 K.314》（1777年）是雙簧管協奏曲文獻的重要作品，展: Mozart's Oboe Concerto K.314 (1777) is a key work in the oboe concerto repertory and shows the instrument's elegant tone. The oboe solo in the second movement of Beethoven's Pastoral Symphony is pastoral in mood. Debussy's Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune is a flute solo, but the oboe's reading of it in later arrangements is just as beguiling. Mahler's symphonies repeatedly use the oboe to create a deep musical atmosphere.
隨著十六世紀樂器製造技術的進步，歐洲工匠開始標準化雙簧樂器的設計，使其音質更為穩: As instrument-making advanced in the sixteenth century, European craftsmen began to standardise the design of double-reed instruments, which made their tone more stable. In the nineteenth century, as concert-hall culture flourished, the oboe became an important member of the symphony orchestra. The establishment of the Hornbostel-Sachs classification gave reed aerophones a firmer scientific standing. Today such instruments are found in cultures around the world, from the old duduk to the oboe of the modern orchestra — a musical inheritance that spans more than a thousand years.
雙簧管主體由歐洲梧桐木（Boxwood）或非洲黑木製成，具有良好的共鳴性能。簧片: The body of the oboe is made of European boxwood or African blackwood, which resonates well. The reed consists of two carefully scraped cane blades, the cane coming from the Camargue in southern France. Cork is used at the joints between the upper and lower sections to keep them airtight. The metal keywork below the toneholes is nickel silver or brass. The pads of the fingerholes are traditionally leather or a synthetic material. On fine instruments the decorative details are sometimes ivory or plastic.
雙簧管音色具有獨特的蘆葦質感，帶有溫潤而略帶鼻音的特性。高音域時音色明亮穿透，具: The oboe's timbre has a distinctive cane texture, warm and slightly nasal. In the high register it is bright and penetrating, with an elegant singing quality; the middle register is the fullest and warmest, and is the instrument's most expressive range; the low register is steady and heavy. The way the double reed vibrates gives its resonance a complex overtone structure, and that is what makes the instrument so recognisable.
